objective: Design and create CustomResourceDefinitions for platform services: OpenAPI schemas, validation rules, defaults, status subresources and versions
secondaryObjectives: Implement workflows for self-service provisioning using platform APIs: composite resources and compositions in Crossplane, or custom resources reconciled by operators

sources.cite: CNCF Certified Cloud Native Platform Engineer (CNPE) curriculum, as the course seed records it: Platform Architecture and Infrastructure 15%, GitOps and Continuous Delivery 25%, Platform APIs and Self-Service Capabilities 25%, Observability and Operations 20%, Security and Policy Enforcement 15%
sources.note: Weights and objective wording are the course seed's (backend/supabase/seed/tracks/cncf-ecosystem.ts). On 2026-11-17 a third-party page (golden-kubestronaut-learning.readthedocs.io/en/latest/cnpe, summarizing fetch) gave different domains (Platform Design 20%, Platform Implementation 30%, Platform Operations 25%, Security and Governance 15%, Developer Experience 10%) with 'GitOps implementation' under Platform Implementation. Which is current is not settled here: to verify against the official curriculum (finding for the verification pass). Reused for REQ-336 from this course's service-selector-no-endpoints-cnpe (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.
The organization, the systems and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You build the internal platform at Quarry Lane Media, a fictional publisher. Tenants open tickets for databases and wait four days. You are designing a PostgresInstance API that tenants create themselves and Crossplane reconciles.
handover: Draft CRD: spec.size as a free string, no validation, no status.
The cloud account has a 2 TB storage policy per database.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: a tenant requests 5 TB; the provider creates it against policy and the monthly bill jumps.
Check-in 3: tenants' apps start before their databases exist and crash-loop; the ticket queue is back.
Check-in 4: 60 existing database claims fail validation; Crossplane stops reconciling them.

schemaPrompt.title: What tenants may ask for
schemaPrompt.context: Free strings reach the cloud provider.

choices.label: An enum size (small, medium, large mapped to 50, 200, 500 GB), CEL validation keeping storage under the 2 TB policy, defaults for version and backups, required fields

effects.log: The schema validates and defaults requests.

choices.feedback: A platform API's schema encodes the rules so bad requests are rejected at the API.

choices.label: Keep free strings and document the allowed values
choices.feedback: Tenants still send 'big'; the composition fails later.

choices.label: Pass any size through to the provider
choices.feedback: A 5 TB request violates the storage policy and runs up cost.

statusPrompt.title: How tenants know it's ready
statusPrompt.context: Tenants can't tell whether provisioning finished.

choices.label: A status subresource with Ready and Synced conditions and a connection secret reference, written by the composition

effects.log: Tenants see Ready and their secret.

choices.feedback: A status subresource reports observed state separately from desired state.

choices.label: Rely on Kubernetes events
choices.feedback: Events expire; tenants can't query readiness reliably.

choices.label: No status: tenants can ask the platform team
choices.feedback: Tenants deploy before the database exists and file tickets anyway.

verPrompt.title: Renaming a field
verPrompt.context: The team wants to rename spec.size to spec.tier.

choices.label: Add v1beta2 with spec.tier, keep v1beta1 served with conversion, and mark it deprecated with a date

effects.log: Both versions are served with conversion.

choices.feedback: CRDs evolve by adding versions and converting, not by breaking stored objects.

choices.label: Accept both fields in v1beta1
choices.feedback: Works, but the API carries confusion forever.

choices.label: Rename the field in place
choices.feedback: Existing claims become invalid; reconciliation of 60 databases fails.

reflection.question: Write the API record for tenants: what they can request, how they see readiness, and how the API will change.

parts.label: Schema and status
parts.criteria: Enum sizes, CEL validation under 2 TB, defaults; Ready and Synced conditions and a secret reference.
parts.modelAnswer: Tenants choose small, medium or large; validation keeps storage under 2 TB; status shows Ready and points to the connection secret.

parts.label: Versions
parts.criteria: v1beta2 with conversion; v1beta1 deprecated with a date.
parts.modelAnswer: spec.tier arrives in v1beta2; v1beta1 stays served with conversion until its deprecation date.

source.note: Service restored and the work closed within 60 minutes of the first report.

scoring.modelReasoning: A platform API is a CRD: its OpenAPI schema, CEL validation and defaults encode the platform's rules; a status subresource reports observed state and connection details; versions evolve with conversion rather than breaking stored objects. Crossplane compositions turn the claim into infrastructure.
